title: Orientation-dependent Pauli noise in one-dimensional discrete-time quantum walks
authors: Alejandro Contreras Reynoso, Adrian Ortega, Thomas Gorin
abstract: Discrete-time quantum walks exhibit ballistic spreading that is highly sensitive to decoherence. We study the long-time dynamics of a one-dimensional discrete-time quantum walk under Pauli noise acting on the coin. Choosing the unitary coin such that its invariant Bloch-sphere axis is orthogonal to the axis fixed by the conditional shift, we identify the distinct effects of noise aligned with either dynamical axis or orthogonal to both. Using a Fourier-space Pauli-superoperator formalism, we derive expressions for the first two position moments and long-time asymptotics for X-, Y-, Z-, and depolarizing noise. All channels induce a crossover from ballistic to diffusive spreading, with a second moment growing linearly at long times. The approach to this regime is channel dependent: it is exponentially fast for X-, Z-, and depolarizing noise, but algebraic, with a leading $t^{-1/2}$ correction, for Y-noise. The position distributions retain distinct finite-noise signatures, including a Gaussian-like profile with a central depression for Y-noise. In the maximal-noise limit, depolarizing, Y-, and Z-noise yield the classical binomial distribution for arbitrary initial coin states, whereas X-noise does so only when the initial state has no component along the noise axis. Thus, the quantum-to-classical transition is governed by the relative alignment of the noise, the coherent walk dynamics, and the initial state.
summary: This paper analyzes how different types of Pauli noise affect the long-time spreading of a quantum walk in one dimension. Using advanced spectral methods in Fourier space, the authors show that noise causes a transition from ballistic to diffusive spreading, with the rate of this transition depending sensitively on the noise's orientation relative to the walk's dynamics. This highlights that the quantum-to-classical transition is highly sensitive to the specific noise mechanism and initial quantum state.
main_problem: The study investigates how the orientation of Pauli noise affects the long-time transport dynamics of a one-dimensional discrete-time quantum walk (DTQW). The goal is to characterize the crossover from ballistic to diffusive spreading under various noise conditions.
main_result: All noise types cause a crossover to diffusive spreading, but the approach rate differs significantly: it is exponentially fast for X-, Z-, and depolarizing noise, while it is algebraic for Y-noise. The quantum-to-classical transition depends critically on the relative alignment of the noise and the initial state.
method: The authors employ a Fourier-space Pauli-superoperator formalism to track the evolution of the quantum state. They calculate position moments and analyze the asymptotic behavior using matrix methods and spectral decomposition.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional DTQW whose evolution is governed by a conditional shift and a coin operation, subjected to Pauli noise acting on the coin. The analysis uses the Fourier basis representation for the density matrix.
key_observables: First two position moments ($\langle x angle, \langle x^2 angle$), probability distribution $P(x, t)$, and the asymptotic behavior of these quantities.
important_parameters: Noise type (X, Y, Z, depolarizing), noise strength ($p$), and time ($t$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the coin's invariant Bloch-sphere axis is orthogonal to the axis fixed by the conditional shift. Calculations rely on approximations for large times and specific spectral decompositions for noise analysis.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares probability distributions for noiseless (ballistic) versus maximal depolarizing noise (diffusive/binomial) over 40 steps using a Hadamard coin.
paper_structure: The paper develops the formalism in Fourier space, derives expressions for moments, analyzes the crossover from ballistic to diffusive regimes based on noise type, and concludes by detailing the conditions governing the quantum-to-classical transition.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed, mathematically rigorous analysis of decoherence effects on quantum transport, which is highly relevant for understanding decoherence in quantum simulators or solid-state quantum devices.
